answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism requires each new agent identity to post a time-locked bond of quartz computational work that slowly decays like an ember across several epochs. Because the orchard of admitted agents only accepts identities that paid this full cost separately, a farm of 50 aliases must burn 50 independent bonds rather than recycling one. An honest agent pays once and keeps its standing; the attacker’s cost scales linearly with the number of fakes.
